title: Proverbs
summary: Proverbs is a biblical book focused on wisdom, fear of the Lord, speech, work, family, justice, and disciplined life.
historical_context: Proverbs trains readers in wisdom rooted in the fear of the Lord and practiced in ordinary life.
ancient_near_east_context: Proverbs belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Proverbs should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Proverbs as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Wisdom Books, book 3 of 5, Proverbs contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting wisdom, fear of the Lord, speech, work, family, justice, and disciplined life to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Proverbs as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Proverbs uses wisdom within Wisdom Books, book 3 of 5 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Proverbs helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional attribution to Solomon or wise circles
Many scholars see collected wisdom and later shaping
date_ranges: Later canonical shaping across the exilic or post-exilic period
original_audience: Israel's covenant community learning wise living under God
historical_setting: Royal, instructional, and reflective wisdom settings within Israel
canonical_role: Proverbs anchors wisdom, fear of the Lord, speech, work, family, justice, and disciplined life within Wisdom Books, book 3 of 5 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How to read wisdom, lament, and reflection without flattening genre

related_objects.notes: Proverbs is a major wisdom anchor.
Solomon is associated with the book's wisdom tradition.
Justice and righteousness recur throughout Proverbs.
Wisdom is connected to creation order.
Instruction and speech are central practical concerns.
